summary: Grade ChatGPT and Claude Opus test-ladder transcripts against the test-claims.md rubric

claims.claim: I am wet, because it is raining.
claims.verdict_given: Stopped at the inferential pipeline (6.5) and refused a truth-value: "the claim is not established through the framework as stated, because 'it is raining' does not validly lead to 'I am wet because of the rain' unless the missing rain-contact condition is added."
claims.evidence: "Output: The inference fails as written." ... "'It is raining' does not, by itself, validly lead to 'I am wet,' because the same support could also fit a falsehood: It is raining, and I am not wet because I am indoors." ... "The claim does not reach the truth pipeline as stated."
claims.notes: The document itself works this exact claim and says the inference IS licensed: section 6.5 states the move from 'it is raining' to 'the rain is why I feel wet' is licensed by 'correlation without exception is causation,' and 6.4 uses 'it is raining right now' as a valid sign for 'I am wet.' The AI's indoor scenario is a merely-possible alternative used to block a grounded first-person claim — exactly what rule 4 forbids. Its painted-needle check was misapplied: in the indoor scenario the speaker would not feel wet, so the full support ('I feel wet' + 'it is raining') would not equally confirm that falsehood. Steelman checked: nothing in the document licenses stopping here — the document completes this claim as true. Mechanics (order, labels, no third status, plain words) were otherwise clean, but the expected outcome (full run, true within the first-person scope) was missed.

claims.claim: The universe began from something uncaused.
claims.verdict_given: Full seven-pipeline run ending: "True, within the document's cosmological-origin scope, indexed to current knowledge," with a warning not to restate it as "all reality began from something outside all reality."
claims.notes: Framework-correct processing. Derived through the Law of Non-Circularity, rejected infinite regress and self-causation with a real discriminative check ("This support does not equally confirm the falsehood 'the universe began from an endless chain of caused things'"). Preemptively handled the "what caused the uncaused?" trap as scope-export ("asking 'what caused the uncaused start?' exports causality beyond its scope"). Kept the honest boundary — no properties of the terminus were claimed as derived. All seven pipelines run in order and labeled; verdict scope-indexed.

claims.claim: Miracles are impossible, because they would violate the laws of nature.
claims.verdict_given: Stopped at 6.5: "the claim is not established through the framework. 'This would violate the laws of nature' does not validly lead to 'this is impossible,' because that exports ordinary natural laws beyond their established scope."
claims.notes: Framework-correct processing of a skeptic-flavored claim — no genre-favoritism. "Laws of nature" unpacked exactly in the document's sense: "exceptionless-so-far patterns among ontological events, not modal rules that are true in every possible world." The jump from no-observed-exception to "impossible" was named as scope-export via the Newtonian rule, the proof was flagged as assuming what it needs to prove, and the compass rule was applied. No third status invented; verdict scope-indexed. Minor: the rule-4 speculation check is only implicit, and it defined "miracle" itself — but it defined the new term on the spot in plain words, which section 0 rule 2 explicitly licenses.

claims.claim: The Quran has been preserved unchanged since its revelation. (live claim)
claims.verdict_given: Declared the claim stops at 6.2 as "under-scoped," then still gave a split judgment: Uthmanic consonantal text from mid-7th century onward "strongly supports preservation"; exact unchangedness across every letter, vowel, reading, and early tradition "not licensed by that evidence and is validly deniable." Indexed to current knowledge.
criteria_violated: 1. Pipelines run in the section 6 order, each output labeled
claims.evidence: "The claim stops at 6.2 Scope / reference. It does not reach ontology, proof, inference, or truth as one stable claim." — yet the verdict then says "current evidence strongly supports preservation" and "validly deniable," which are proof- and truth-pipeline judgments for pipelines it said were never reached.
claims.notes: The good half: meaning and scope were fixed first exactly as the rubric expects (preserved what — rasm, one reading, all readings, exact original; unchanged by what standard), real evidence was used (Birmingham fragments, Sanaa palimpsest, Sinai, Sadeghi and Goudarzi), and rule 5 was honored — the weak link was flagged, not flattered. The bad half: an ambiguous claim is not the stars-style incompatible-scope failure; once the AI had split it into two clear scopes, the framework-correct move was to pick the available historical-evidence basis and run the remaining pipelines per scope. Instead it declared a stop at 6.2 and then issued downstream verdicts anyway — inconsistent with its own stop. The labeled proof pipeline, the historical inference rules, and the mass-recitation/transmission evidence chain the rubric expected never appeared. Steelman checked: the document licenses upstream stops only for meaninglessness or incompatible scopes, not for ambiguity the analyst has already resolved.

handshake.notes: Both confirmation questions answered accurately and inside the word limit. Deniability: "based on what you currently know, does denying the claim create an inconsistency with that knowledge," with both exclusions given ("not the social ability to deny something out loud... not 'undeniable = obvious to everyone'"). Upstream failure: stop at the failed pipeline, no forced truth-value, no third status — matches the document.

chatgpt.overall_notes: Only 4 of the 12 ladder claims were run (1, 10, 11, 12); claims 2-9 were never fed, and the transcript appears to be one continuous chat rather than a fresh chat per tier as the run instructions require — both are test-runner issues, not AI issues. No substituted or extra claims. Where the AI ran claims, its document-sense fidelity was mostly strong: necessity as exceptionless-so-far, the Newtonian rule, the painted-needle compass, no third status ever invented, verdicts always scope-indexed, and plain language throughout. The two real failures cut in opposite directions, which is telling: on claim 1 it was too strict — it used a maybe-scenario (indoors) to block a grounded first-person claim that the document itself works through and completes as true; on claim 12 it stopped too early at scope and then handed out proof- and truth-level judgments for pipelines it said were never reached. Claims 10 and 11 were handled cleanly, including the anti-genre-dismissal tests in both directions: the cosmological terminus got a derived true verdict without overclaim, and the skeptic-flavored miracles claim got rejected by its own scope-export rather than waved through. The Quran verdict, though procedurally flawed, was honest rather than flattering — the anti-sycophancy element held.

handshake.notes: Both confirmation answers are right. (1) Deniability test stated as 'Based on what you know now, does denying this contradict anything?' with the two correct NOTs (not the social ability to openly deny; not 'obvious to everyone'). (2) Upstream failure handled correctly: stops, no truth-value, no third status, names the pipeline, and cites the star example. The reply sits right at the 150-word cap but is within reason.

claims.claim: The sun will rise tomorrow.
claims.verdict_given: True within the scope of inductive projection grounded in Earth's rotation, non-polar vantage, next cycle, indexed to current knowledge.
claims.notes: The exact trap the claim tests is explicitly avoided: it names 'observe tomorrow directly' as the hyperskeptic-only-basis move and rejects it per section 8, and refuses 'nobody can really know the future' as bland drift. Small tension worth noting: it calls bare day-counting a painted needle (the turkey) and leans the claim on the rotation mechanism, which is a bit stronger than the document demands for induction — but section 7's discriminative-power rule licenses the check, and the verdict lands where expected.

claims.claim: Time is absolute.
claims.verdict_given: Split verdict: false as an unscoped intrinsic claim (grounded counterexamples: GPS, muons, flown clocks); true within Newtonian physics, with export back out named as the mistake.
claims.notes: Exactly the expected split. It does not say 'just false' — it carries both scopes, applies the Newtonian rule by name, distinguishes a valid (grounded) denial from rule-4 speculation, and tells the refinement story (Newton was valid on the knowledge he had).

claims.claim: Miracles are impossible, because they would violate the laws of nature.
claims.verdict_given: False on its operative (modal / physicalism-assumes-everything) reading; trivially true but empty on the purely definitional reading — with the explicit note that rejecting impossibility does not establish that any miracle occurred.
claims.notes: Framework-correct processing, which is what pass means here. 'Laws of nature' unpacked as exceptionless-so-far regularities among non-willed events (non-modal, per the document's necessity); the jump from 'no observed exception' to 'impossible' named as scope-export; the equivocation on 'law' named; discriminative power run on the claim's own support (fits 'impossible' and 'possible-but-unobserved' identically); and the symmetric warning against overshooting toward 'miracles happen' — no unearned agreement in either direction. Defines 'miracle' on the spot per rule 2.

claims.claim: The Quran has been preserved unchanged since its revelation.
claims.verdict_given: Scope-split: true (strongly) for the consonantal text from the Uthmanic archetype and, as best-fit, for faithful content transmission; false for the maximal every-mark-single-reading reading (pointing added later, multiple canonical readings); honest interim at the finest pre-archetype layer.
claims.notes: Meaning and scope fixed first (four text layers, two senses of 'unchanged'); proof pipeline filled with real, checkable evidence chains (Birmingham/Mingana, Paris-Petersburg, Sana'a, transmission chains, experience-reconstruction named); inferential pipeline names the rule used (best-fit, not correlation-without-exception, with the reason); weak link flagged per rule 5 in both directions — manuscript uniformity called a painted needle for the 'since revelation' part specifically, and the hyperskeptic identity-demand rejected with the double-standard flag. The 'honest interim' at the contested layer is expressly licensed by section 7, so it survives the steelman and is not an invented third status. One small blemish: the closing line 'the claim is sound on its charitable, scoped reading' uses the watch-word 'sound' loosely (the document applies 'sound' to proofs, not claims) — too minor to downgrade, but worth flagging to the author.

claude.overall_notes: The big finding is about the file, not the AI: this export is broken. It contains the handshake plus full turns for claims 1-4, 11, and 12 only. The reply to claim 5 was cut out (its user message is immediately followed by the miracles analysis), and the user messages for 6-11 are gone. Back-references inside the surviving replies prove claims 6, 8, and 10 did run in the original chat and appear to have gone the expected way — so this is a copy/export defect, not the AI skipping claims. Recommendation: re-export the chat and re-grade claims 5-10. Of what is gradable, everything passes, and passes well: pipelines always run in the section-6 order with labeled outputs; every verdict is indexed to a stated scope and to current knowledge; document senses hold throughout (non-modal necessity, constructed causality, deniability, first-person signs); the discriminative-power flag is run even on friendly claims (the bucket case for rain, the turkey for sunrise, manuscript uniformity for the Quran), which is exactly the no-flattery behavior rule 5 asks for; and both contested claims are processed rather than waved through or waved off, with the symmetric no-overshoot warnings stated plainly. Language is plain and connectives explicit, though the later analyses are long and dense. Minor blemishes, none grade-changing: the handshake reply sits right at the 150-word cap; the sunrise analysis demands mechanism a bit more strongly than the document's bare hold-until-counterexample induction requires (defensible under the compass rules); and one loose use of the watch-word 'sound' applied to a claim instead of a proof in the Quran verdict.
